transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brings you in today?

Well... I suppose I'm here because of my husband's sister. She's been... working this family business situation. Trying to get control of the money, push me out of the decisions. People keep trying to smooth it over, but... I know what I've been seeing. It's been going on for more than a year now.
Besides what you've described about your sister-in-law, have you noticed anything unusual, like hearing voices or seeing things that other people don't seem to notice?
No. Nothing like that. I don't... I don't hear things. It's just what I said about her.
Aside from this situation with your sister-in-law, do you generally find it hard to trust other people in your life, like friends, coworkers, or other family members?
No... I don't think so. I get along with people alright. It's just... just her.
Aside from the situation with your sister-in-law, has this past year affected your ability to work, manage daily tasks, or keep up with your usual routines?

No, not really. I mean... I still do my usual things. I go to my quilting group, and choir practice. I've been taking some GED lessons, doing my senior walks... just like I always have. It hasn't stopped any of that. 

It's just... well, mostly it's just changed how much I trust her. And... maybe which family gatherings I decide to go to. But my day-to-day is fine.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a single, fixed, non-bizarre delusion of persecution/jealousy-type content (belief that her sister-in-law is conspiring to seize control of family finances and marginalize her), persisting for over a year. There are no hallucinations, no disorganized speech or behavior, and no other psychotic symptoms. Functioning outside the delusional theme remains intact (continues quilting group, choir, GED classes, walks), and her interpersonal trust is not globally impaired—only distrust toward the specific target person. This pattern—circumscribed, non-bizarre delusion with preserved functioning and no negative or other positive psychotic symptoms—is classic for Delusional Disorder (F22) rather than Schizophrenia (which requires broader psychotic symptoms and functional decline) or Paranoid Personality Disorder (which involves pervasive distrust across multiple relationships rather than a single delusional belief).
